note: Generated from CHANGELOG.md by `go run ./scripts/whatchanged -gen`; do not edit by hand. The grammar is in docs/releasing.md.

changes.summary: A fleetfetch client (and the server.New safehttp cache delegate) with no limit now cuts response bodies at 32 MiB and sets Response.Truncated; they were read whole before.
changes.off_switch: FLEET_FETCH_MAX_BODY_BYTES=<bytes>, or 0 for no limit (discouraged), in the environment; WithMaxBodyBytes(n) or WithUnboundedBody() in code

changes.summary: WithMaxBodyBytes(n <= 0) no longer means unlimited: it is ignored and the 32 MiB default stays. Unlimited is WithUnboundedBody() only.
changes.off_switch: WithUnboundedBody() in code, or FLEET_FETCH_MAX_BODY_BYTES=0 in the environment

changes.summary: A request under a declared PublicPathPrefixes entry, or for a fixed probe path, with a non-canonical path (dot segments, //, encoded . / \) now gets 400 from the gate instead of skipping auth.
a `route` or `host` label value that is not valid UTF-8 or is over 256 bytes counts under `_other` (it panicked, or was kept for the life of the process).
`scheme` on `safehttp_egress_requests_total` is `http`, `https` or `_other` instead of whatever scheme the URL had.
`status` on `http_requests_total` folds codes that are not registered into their class (`499` becomes `4xx`) and codes outside 100-599 into `_other`.
`primitive` and `suffix` on `fleet_degraded_total` take at most 64 and 16 values per process; the rest count under `_other`.
`safehttp_egress_duration_seconds` and `fleet_fetch_cache_age_seconds` lose their `host` label: a query that filters or groups them by `host` now gets one series per service.
`host` on `safehttp_egress_requests_total`, `safehttp_egress_response_bytes_total` and `fleet_fetch_total` takes at most 32 named values per process (was 256); every other host counts under `_other`.
changes.off_switch: for an `EgressCollectors` a service builds itself, `promx.WithHostLimit(256)` and `promx.WithHostMinHits(1)` restore the old naming; `fleet_fetch_total` takes no setting

changes.summary: `go.mod` says `go 1.26.0`: a service that adopts this release needs a Go 1.26 builder (`golang:1.26` or newer), and `go get` raises its own `go` line to 1.26.0.
changes.off_switch: stay on 0.103.x; `scripts/backport.sh` cuts a `release/0.103` line only when a real service needs a security fix (docs/releasing.md)

changes.summary: `server.New` sends fleet-internal destinations (container names, private and tailnet addresses, our domains) direct on `http.DefaultTransport`; the rest still follows `HTTP_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY`.
changes.off_switch: `FLEET_EGRESS_DEFAULT_TRANSPORT=off` (also `false`, `0`, `no`, `disabled`) in the service's environment, no release needed

changes.summary: the `promx` HTTP metrics label a request `method="OTHER"` when its method is not one of the nine standard ones: a dashboard or alert that selects a non-standard method by name must select `"OTHER"`.
`server.Run`/`RunTier` now log the error from `Server.Start` and exit with status 1 (before: status 0, no message), so a restart-on-failure policy restarts a service whose port is taken.
`client.Fetch` and `jsbundle.Recover`/`RecoverAll` return an error instead of panicking when proxy egress is required and no proxy variable is set; a caller that relied on the panic must check it.
`safehttp.IsBlocked` (so `GuardHost`, `CheckURL`, the guarded dialer, `egressproxy.DefaultGuard`) also refuses IPv6 addresses that carry a blocked IPv4 address through NAT64 or 6to4.
`jsbundle.RecoverOptions.Client`, when nil, is a guarded `safehttp` client (20 s timeout, refuses internal addresses) instead of `http.DefaultClient`.
changes.off_switch: set `RecoverOptions.Client` (for example an `httptest` server's client in a test)

changes.summary: `validate`'s `pattern=` tag now requires the whole value to match (it was applied unanchored): a tag that relied on substring matching starts rejecting.
`GRAPH_USE_EGRESS_PROXY` is removed and `graph` is always direct: only a service on 0.102.59 that set it is affected (nothing used it).
`server/mcp.go`'s MCP bridge copied any request header a caller sent into the replayed request; it now forwards only an explicit allowlist of headers.
`obs` is opt-in: `server.New` no longer starts the localhost pprof and `/metrics` debug server (127.0.0.1:6060); a service that wants it calls `obs.Init()` in `main()`.
changes.off_switch: `stop, _ := obs.Init()` and `defer stop()` in `main()` bring the old debug server back
